title: Afternoon kernel triage & perf scratchpad (Lina)
linked_artifacts: confluence:Serving Runtime KV eviction experiment notes
content:
Context:
- Quick afternoon dump while triaging two recurring incidents: higher p95 on short-chat workloads and intermittent kv-cache evictions causing 10-40ms tail spikes.
- Repro window: small-batch, <32 tokens, high QPS (~1200 rps per GPU). Observed spikes around token 1-3 when requests hit cold kv-cache or eviction occurs during burst.

What I saw (timeline):
- 12:30: alerted on p95 jump for model: redwood-small-v2 in eu-west1-host-3. Dashboard shows CPU on CPU-bound helper thread spikes, GPU throughput unchanged.
- 12:34: rolled canary to older kernel (kexec trick) — p95 dropped back but not to baseline.
- 12:50: attached perf trace (perf script + simple flamegraph) from host-3. Hot function: kv_cache::maybe_evict_and_sync and spin on eviction lock.
- 13:05: reproduction locally with opt-runner (qps=1200, batch cap 4) reproduced tail spikes; setting KV_MAX_BYTES to 1.2x base reduced spikes but increased memory usage.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction algorithm degenerates under frequent short sequences because prefix cache keys get churned fast -> lock contention on global eviction list.
2) Background compaction thread and request threads sometimes contend due to heavy allocator activity; observed >50% time in jemalloc arena lock.
3) Pathological kernel preemption during small token output; unlikely since GPU idle unchanged.

Quick reproduction notes (commands):
- repro script (local): ./scripts/repro_short_chat.sh --qps 1200 --batch-cap 4 --seq 24 --model redwood-small-v2
- perf capture: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./bin/runtime --config local-debug.yaml; sudo perf script > out.folded; ./scripts/flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
- trace logs: RUNTIME_TRACE=kv,alloc ./bin/runtime --config ... > trace.kv

What I tried and results:
- bump KV_MAX_BYTES by +20%: p95 reduces 12–20ms, but memory footprint per host rises ~1.8GB at 4k QPS.
- disabled background compaction: small improvement, but memory gradually increases; not sustainable.
- switched jemalloc to tcmalloc in dev image: tail spikes reduced in local repro but needs benchmarking for fragmentation.
- quick patch (WIP) to change eviction list from global lock to sharded locks (4 shards): local run shows much lower contention in perf. Patch location: PR #1423.

Open TODOs (short term):
- [ ] Add diagnostic to expose per-shard eviction queue length and last-eviction-timestamp (logs + metrics). (owner: Lina, due EOD)
- [ ] Run full cluster perf test with sharded-eviction patch on a canary pool (20 hosts) and capture p50/p95/p99 for short-chat profile. (owner: Diego, due 2024-11-12)
- [ ] Try tcmalloc benchmark on staging fleet to validate fragmentation + latency tradeoffs (owner: Mina, due 2024-11-14)
- [ ] Add jemalloc stats exporter to host-metrics for immediate visibility (owner: Lina, due 2024-11-10)
- [ ] Draft fallback policy: if eviction pressure > X and memory > Y, route short sequences to variant with KV disabled (owner: product/hosted-api, PR reference).

Longer notes / ideas:
- Consider moving small-sequence hot-path to per-connection tiny cache (bounded by count, not bytes) to avoid touching global eviction machinery for the most frequent short chats. Might trade accuracy for latency.
- Potential micro-optimization: avoid atomic refcount ops on prefix keys during write path by deferring acks to batching thread. Risk: memory leak if crash; need robust accounting.
- Think about using eBPF to sample kernel-level syscalls for allocator hotspots; quick perf shows high syscall counts around allocation/free during eviction bursts.

Observations for incident writeup:
- Key symptom: p95 spikes align with periods of rapid small-sequence churn (many unique prefixes in short window).
- Primary signal in perf: stack traces dominated by eviction and allocator locks, not model forward path.
- Temporary mitigations: bump KV_MAX_BYTES, restrict QPS burst throttle, or route to older kernel. Each has cost (memory, throughput, rollout complexity).

Notes to self (next steps):
- pair with Diego tomorrow 09:30am to run canary test and look at jemalloc/tcmalloc comparison dashboards.
- push WIP sharded-eviction branch into test harness; add tests that simulate worst-case churn (random prefix ids, TTL expiry).
- capture heap profiles during steady-state and during replication of burst to compare fragmentation.

Small snippets / patches to remember:
- quick coarse-lock -> shard map change: use fixed-size vector<mutex> and map prefix_hash % N to shard. Don't forget to pre-allocate to avoid rehashing.
- metric: runtime.kv.evictions_per_minute_shard_{i} and runtime.kv.shard_queue_len_{i}

Questions / unknowns to follow up on:
- How often do user prefixes collide between requests vs truly unique ones in production short-chat workload? Is client-side batching causing false uniqueness?
- Is there a correlation between GC cycles (managed languages in auxiliary processes) and jemalloc stalls? Need host-wide timeline correlation.

Random quick notes (brain dump):
- If sharded approach holds, we can try adaptive shard count based on CPU cores; maybe 2x cores as initial.
- Also check whether our kernel's futex implementation has regressions in the new Ubuntu kernel (we rolled images last month). Cross-validate with kernel version on hosts that show problems.

End of dump.

Small log of commands run during session:
- git checkout -b improve/kv-sharded-evict && edit src/kv/evict.cpp
- ./scripts/repro_short_chat.sh --qps 1200 --batch-cap 4 --seq 16
- sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep runtime) -- sleep 30; sudo perf report --stdio | head -n 40

If I forget: follow-up list pinned in Slack #eng-serving-runtime under thread p95-2024-11-08.
